h: Art, squirrels and a sky full of stars
p: Kielder isn't just trees and water. Dotted around the lake and forest are pieces of art and architecture that turn a walk or ride into a bit of a treasure hunt. The most famous is Kielder Skyspace by James Turrell, a stone chamber with an opening in the roof that frames the sky. Sit inside for a while and you'll see why people rave about it.

Wildlife lovers are in for a treat too. The forest is a stronghold for red squirrels, so walk quietly through the trees and keep your eyes up. Ospreys nest in the area during the warmer months, and you might spot deer if you're out early or late in the day.

Then there are the stars. Kielder sits within the Northumberland International Dark Sky Park, and on a clear night the Milky Way is a jaw-dropper. Kielder Observatory runs stargazing events, but they're separate from the forest and need booking well in advance.

Practicalities matter here. Mobile signal is patchy, fuel stations are few, and the drive in takes longer than you'd think, so fill up beforehand and download maps. Summer midges can be lively, so pack repellent. Give the trip a full day at least, or better still, stay over in a cabin or lodge nearby and do it properly.
On the way back to Hexham, you're never far from Hadrian's Wall country, and Hexham Abbey in the heart of town is well worth a look if you've got any energy left.
